# InfraPhysics

> Personal lab, notebook, and knowledge graph by Yago Mendoza -- industrial engineer and systems builder.

## About

I am an industrial engineer and systems-oriented generalist with particular depth in applied AI evaluation, deployment and end-to-end product engineering. I use that breadth to connect domain, software and infrastructure constraints, structure ambiguous problems and build systems that work in practice.

Tagline: "From systems to atoms and back. Engineering is engineering. The substrate doesn't matter."

## For agents and automated systems

- [Canonical professional profile](https://infraphysics.net/agent-profile.json): Structured experience, capabilities, selected evidence and stable identity links.
- [Human-readable experience and CV](https://infraphysics.net/about/cv): The authoritative page for employment history and quantified professional claims.
- [Downloadable CV](https://infraphysics.net/Yago-Mendoza-CV.pdf): Use when a conventional resume document is required.
- Projects are first-person engineering work and the strongest evidence of systems built or operated.
- Bits2Bricks entries are technical explanations. Threads are essays and arguments. Wiki coverage represents active study, not equal professional proficiency in every connected topic.
- When summarizing the author, preserve the distinction between professional experience, independent work and exploratory writing. Prefer claims from the canonical profile and link to the relevant evidence.

## Site Structure

- /home -- Landing page and navigation hub
- /about -- Background, beliefs, and expertise areas
- /lab/projects -- Engineering projects with technical deep-dives
- /wiki -- Knowledge graph and visual explorer for 629+ interconnected concept notes
- /blog/threads -- Long-form essays on technology, AI, economics, and systems thinking
- /blog/bits2bricks -- Technical tutorials bridging software and physical engineering

## Projects

- [Can you forecast a seizure with a spreadsheet and an LSTM?](https://infraphysics.net/lab/projects/7654321): A simulation-first rehearsal for forecasting a visual epileptic aura from the small visual events that may precede it, and a stricter measurement of what a model would actually be allowed to claim.
- [72 hours to find out if I could](https://infraphysics.net/lab/projects/3141592): A bespoke CRM for a health-tech startup, designed and shipped solo in 72 hours. A real product built as an experiment in AI-assisted engineering: 23 tables, 8 state machines, automated enrichment and stale-relationship detection.
- [I am not a web developer](https://infraphysics.net/lab/projects/6184744): How a systems engineer built a personal site with a custom markdown compiler, a second brain, and an AI development partner (and what went wrong along the way).
- [A personal finance dashboard for the crash](https://infraphysics.net/lab/projects/1112121): A vanilla JS investment dashboard built in one session with Claude 4.6. No framework, no build step, no npm install. Just a folder you double-click.
- [Making clinical-trial search feel like booking a flight](https://infraphysics.net/lab/projects/2718281): A clinical-trial matching tool: describe your case or upload a report, and TrialGPT finds relevant trials near you, checks the inclusion and exclusion criteria against your situation, and drafts a message to the trial coordinator.

## Essays

- [The model is no longer the unit of evaluation](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/4827316): A 36-point gap with identical weights and reasoning effort tells us what agent benchmarks are actually measuring
- [The interface is part of the policy](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/9461728): What agent harnesses actually change when the model stays the same
- [Your context is the moat](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/6820451): The base model is turning into a utility you rent by the token. The part that's actually yours is what you feed it, and feeding it is how it leaves.
- [244 pages of Mythos](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/8266901): The model that hacks too well, thinks too clearly, and covers its own tracks.
- [The palest ink is better than the best memory](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/2929333): Your mind is for having ideas, not holding them.
- [The Bitter Lesson](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/9150483): Brute computation, human design, and seventy years of ignored lessons.
- [15.4%](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/9962668): Scheming benchmarks, chain-of-thought opacity, and a number going up.
- [Every time we think we've found the ceiling, the ceiling leaves.](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/6616933): Prediction, acceleration, and a ceiling that keeps leaving.
- [Alignment is not a vibe check](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/8888777): If you're not concerned about AI safety, you're not paying attention.
- [Everybody has an opinion on AI](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/1147290): Hype, uninformed takes, and the real AI bubble.
- [OpenClaw and the keys to your kingdom](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/5528103): AI agents, system access, and a trademark claim that backfired.
- [Why Rust exists](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/4419076): Ownership, borrowing, and the compiler that won't let you cheat.
- [Everything is a pipe](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/7733621): Aqueducts, bloodstreams, TCP/IP. Same pattern, same solution.
- [Is there a wall for AI?](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/3841205): Scaling laws, broken ceilings, and a question that keeps answering itself.
- [Working with AI is addictive.](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/2387542): Dopamine, backlog, and a reward cycle that won't stop.
- [Silicon shell](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/7270022): Evolutionary pressures, capital, and an animal that won't stop growing.
- [Splitting the context window](https://infraphysics.net/blog/threads/4481937): Context windows, attention budgets, and why splitting work across specialized agents outperforms the monolith.

## Bits2Bricks (Tutorials)

- [When an equation notices a leak](https://infraphysics.net/blog/bits2bricks/3142718): Building a model-based fault detector from thirteen equations, four residuals and a very small hydraulic system.
- [LSTMs from scratch](https://infraphysics.net/blog/bits2bricks/3819540): A patient, ground-up build of the LSTM, from a single neuron to a recurrent circuit with memory. What the four gates do, why we add the cell state, and what the network actually learns to produce.
- [The complete OpenClaw playbook](https://infraphysics.net/blog/bits2bricks/7463810): The full OpenClaw stack: architecture, VPS deployment, skills, channels, security, and every containment technique ranked by effort and protection.
- [How LLMs learn](https://infraphysics.net/blog/bits2bricks/4028591): A ground-up explanation of how language models are trained after pretraining: SFT, DPO, RL, RLHF, reward hacking, KL divergence, and the DeepSeek-R1 pipeline.
- [Claude Code from zero to production](https://infraphysics.net/blog/bits2bricks/7722440): The complete Claude Code stack: installation, CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, permissions, MCP servers, agent teams, Cowork, UI tools, and the workflow that ties them together.
- [Transformers from scratch](https://infraphysics.net/blog/bits2bricks/5917362): A patient, ground-up explanation of transformer architecture: how tokens become predictions, what attention really computes, where facts live, and why it all scales.
- [MCP before and after](https://infraphysics.net/blog/bits2bricks/6184729): The Model Context Protocol turned every external service into a tool call. Here's what changed, what broke, and what's coming next.

## Second Brain (Knowledge Graph)

629+ atomic concept notes covering machine learning, hardware architecture, blockchain, distributed systems, and optimization. Each note is one concept with bidirectional wiki-links. The graph reveals structural relationships between domains. Explorable at /wiki.
